dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For indices i and j in a type with decidable equality, this is the real Kronecker delta δ(i,j), equal to 1 when i = j and 0 otherwise.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Scaled by L, it defines the matrix Lδ on Fin m ⊔ Fin n, whose quadratic form is L times the sum of the squares of all coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For two real matrices A and B on the same finite index type, it states that q_A(x) ≤ q_B(x) for every real vector x, where q_A(x) = Σ_i x_i Σ_j A_ij x_j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the right side of the equivalence the universal quadratic-form inequality q_{B_M}(z) ≤ q_{Lδ}(z).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: It states that for every x in ℝ^n, the Euclidean norm of Ax is at most L times the Euclidean norm of x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is exactly the left side of the target equivalence, with A = M.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: It defines a matrix B_M on Fin m ⊔ Fin n by B_M(inl i,inr j) = M_ij, B_M(inr j,inl i) = M_ij, and B_M = 0 on the two same-summand blocks.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a finite square matrix A and vector x, it computes Σ_i x_i(Ax)_i = Σ_i Σ_j x_i A_ij x_j.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007

binders: m and n are arbitrary natural numbers, including zero.
M is an arbitrary real m-by-n matrix represented by entries M_ij for i in Fin m and j in Fin n.
L is an arbitrary real number.
In the left-hand assertion, x ranges universally over all real vectors indexed by Fin n.
In the right-hand assertion, z ranges universally over all real vectors indexed by I = Fin m ⊔ Fin n; equivalently, z consists of arbitrary u in ℝ^m and v in ℝ^n.
conclusions: The assertion that every x in ℝ^n satisfies ||Mx||₂ ≤ L||x||₂ is logically equivalent to the assertion that every z indexed by Fin m ⊔ Fin n satisfies q_{B_M}(z) ≤ q_{Lδ}(z).
Writing z = (u,v), the right-hand assertion is equivalently: for every u in ℝ^m and v in ℝ^n, 2 Σ_i Σ_j u_i M_ij v_j ≤ L(Σ_i u_i^2 + Σ_j v_j^2).
mathematical_definitions: For x indexed by Fin n, (Mx)_i = Σ_{j in Fin n} M_ij x_j.
For any finite real vector y, ||y||₂ = sqrt(Σ_i y_i^2).
Let I = Fin m ⊔ Fin n and δ(a,b) = 1 when a = b and 0 otherwise.
Define B_M on I by B_M(inl i,inr j) = M_ij, B_M(inr j,inl i) = M_ij, B_M(inl i,inl i') = 0, and B_M(inr j,inr j') = 0.
For a matrix A on a finite index set and a vector y, q_A(y) = Σ_a y_a(Σ_b A_ab y_b) = Σ_a Σ_b y_a A_ab y_b.
The comparison matrix has entries (Lδ)_ab = Lδ(a,b), so q_{Lδ}(z) = LΣ_a z_a^2.
If u_i = z(inl i) and v_j = z(inr j), then q_{B_M}(z) = 2Σ_iΣ_j u_i M_ij v_j.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite real m-by-n matrix M and every nonnegative real number L, M maps every vector x to a vector whose Euclidean norm is at most L times the Euclidean norm of x if and only if the symmetric block matrix with zero diagonal blocks and off-diagonal blocks M and Mᵀ has quadratic form at most L times the squared Euclidean norm on every combined vector (u,v).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is conditional on 0 ≤ L and makes no assertion for negative L.
The dimensions m and n may be zero. If either dimension is zero, both sides are automatically true under 0 ≤ L, so the equivalence is degenerate.
All spaces are finite-dimensional and real; no complex, infinite-dimensional, or non-Euclidean version is encoded.
L is only asserted to be an upper bound. The proposition does not state that L is minimal, attained, or equal to an operator norm.
The right side encodes a one-sided universal quadratic-form inequality, not an explicitly absolute-valued inequality or an equality.
Empty finite sums are interpreted as zero.
